content.text: Correction: on an existing thread, a `pr_number` run is sent as a follow-up (the `first` flag is `thread.isNew && handled.size === 0`), so its diff is not re-sent. I'll document that precisely.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/prompts.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="""| **First message** | The first request of a new thread, and each `pr_number` run or direct prompt on a new thread | The built-in prompt, or your `prompt_template` |
| **Follow-up** | Each later `@pi` comment on the thread | `**@login** commented (<url>):` and the task. For a review comment: `commented on the diff` |"""
new="""| **First message** | The first request of a new thread. A direct prompt always has a new thread | The built-in prompt, or your `prompt_template` |
| **Follow-up** | Each later request on the thread: an `@pi` comment, or a `pr_number` run | `**@login** commented (<url>):` and the task. For a review comment: `commented on the diff`. pi-action adds the URL when it has one |"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="A follow-up does not repeat the issue or the diff, because the thread already has them. See [Durable threads](threads.md)."
new="A follow-up does not repeat the issue or the diff, because the thread already has them. Thus, when a pull request gets new commits, pi does not get a new diff automatically. Ask pi to look at the changes (for example, `@pi review the new commits`): its tools can run `git` and `gh`. See [Durable threads](threads.md)."
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='docs/workflows.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="- Without `prompt`, the task is `Please review this pull request`."
new="- Without `prompt`, the task is `Please review this pull request`.\n- The diff and the description go into the first message of a new thread only. When the thread of the pull request exists, the run sends only the task as a [follow-up](prompts.md). pi can get the new diff with its tools."
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
